{"name":"Tariq","message":"No problem—since you can’t assist directly, here’s a ready‑to‑use rapid auth troubleshooting pack you can drop to the on‑call or incident channel. No response needed.

Rapid triage (first 10–15 minutes)
- Identify scope: Is it all users or subset? All apps or specific (SSO SAML/OIDC, VPN/RADIUS, on‑prem AD/LDAP)? Since when did impact start?
- Check provider health: IdP/MFA/VPN status pages and your admin dashboard for incidents or rate limits.
- Clock/NTP: Clock skew breaks Kerberos, SAML, and JWT. Verify time sync on IdP, domain controllers, VPN/RADIUS.
  - Windows DC: w32tm /query /status; if skewed → w32tm /resync /force
  - Linux: timedatectl status; chronyc tracking (or ntpstat); if skewed → sudo systemctl restart chronyd or ntpd
- Certificates/keys: Confirm TLS and SAML signing certs not expired; confirm OIDC secrets not rotated and redirect URIs unchanged.
  - TLS: openssl s_client -connect sso.example.com:443 -servername sso.example.com </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -issuer -subject
  - AD FS: Get-AdfsCertificate -CertificateType Token-Signing; Get-AdfsSslCertificate
- Blast radius tests: Try 1 known‑good admin account and 1 affected account. Compare results.
- Network/DNS: From affected network, verify DNS and reachability to IdP endpoints.
  - dig +short idp.example.com; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{remote_ip}\n" https://idp.example.com

If SAML SSO is failing
- Capture one failing SAMLResponse (use browser devtools Network tab or SAML‑tracer). Redact PII.
- Decode and validate:
  - base64 decode → check NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter timestamps (clock skew), Audience matches SP entityID, ACS URL exact match, Issuer correct.
  - Signature present and valid; signing cert not expired and thumbprint matches IdP.
- Common breakages and quick fixes:
  - Audience/ACS mismatch after app update → update SP config or IdP app settings.
  - Expired signing cert → upload new cert to SP and IdP; align rollover window.
  - Clock skew → fix NTP on IdP/DC.

If OIDC/OAuth is failing
- Validate discovery and endpoints:
  - curl -s https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq '.issuer, .authorization_endpoint, .token_endpoint'
  - Ensure app uses the same issuer; check redirect URIs are exact.
- Token checks:
  - Inspect id_token aud/iss/exp/nbf; confirm JWKs kid matches; confirm clock skew not negative.
- Frequent errors and actions:
  - invalid_client → secret rotated or wrong client_id/secret.
  - redirect_uri_mismatch → app changed URI; update in IdP.
  - invalid_grant/interaction_required → consent/MFA/conditional access blocking.

If VPN/RADIUS is failing
- Shared secret and DC reachability are top causes.
- Test RADIUS locally:
  - radtest user pass radius.example.com 0 testing123 (FreeRADIUS)
  - freeradius -X to see live logs (lab only)
- Windows NPS: Event Viewer → Custom Views → Server Roles → Network Policy and Access Services; look for reject reasons.
- On AD side, check Security logs around a failed attempt: 4625 (failed logon), 4771 (Kerberos pre‑auth), 4776 (NTLM).

If on‑prem AD/Kerberos/LDAP is failing
- Account health: lockouts/disablement/password expired.
- DC health:
  - nltest /dclist:yourdomain; dcdiag; repadmin /replsummary
  - Kerberos cache issues: klist purge (client), check time sync.

Minimal‑risk mitigations while investigating
- Roll back the last auth‑related change (app config, cert, secret, policy) if within the change window.
- Temporarily exclude a test group from a newly deployed conditional access/MFA policy to confirm blast radius.
- If supported, enable fail‑open for non‑critical apps only; document and time‑box it.

Data to collect (single example failure)
- UTC timestamp, username (or a placeholder), app name/URL, flow type (SAML/OIDC/VPN), client IP/network, and exact error text/screenshot.
- IdP/App logs for that timestamp; attach SAMLResponse or OIDC error payload (redacted).

Comms templates
- User notice (generic):

- Incident update (internal):

Decision tree to isolate quickly

- I can also draft a rollback or policy exclusion plan with explicit blast radius and risk notes.
